New Supper Club To Highlight the Hobby Center’s Sweeping $45 Million Makeover — Creating a Dynamic Scene Worthy of Lincoln Center

New Capital Campaign Is Already $31 Million In and Major Changes Are Coming

By Shelby Hodge // Nov 2, 2026

1/8

Hobby Center for the Performing Arts is doing a $41 million capital campaign and a new performance space — a supper club (Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

The new supper club theater at the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts is anticipated to open fall 2028

Cocktail tables for two as envisioned for the new performance space in the Hobby Center.

The two-tiered theater will host 160 theater-goers (Photo by Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

The new club at the Hobby Center will preserve the unique skyline view of downtown Houston (Photo by Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

Enhanced hospitality areas such as the Kades Club are part of the Hobby Center's $41 million capital campaign plan (Photo by Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

Enhanced hospitality areas such as the Kades Club entry are part of the Hobby Center's $41 million capital campaign plan (Photo by Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

Sarofim Hall at the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts has upgraded technology and fittings as part of the 2026 capital campaign (Photo by Courtesy of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts)

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:57
Instaread

The curtain rose Monday night on a new chapter for the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts with the reveal of a $45 million capital campaign geared around elevating the 24-year-old center across performance spaces and visitor experience, and funding an exciting third performance venue. Think an inmate supper club a la The Carlisle.

Campaign chairs Lesha and Tom Elsenbrook announced the effort at festivities for supporters in the Hobby Center’s Founder’s Club, which closes in April 2027. It will reopen fall 2028 as an elegant supper club featuring a broad swath of top tier entertainers.

“So this is a new kind of supper club experience for Houston. I love that idea,” Hobby Center president and CEO Mark Folkes tells PaperCity. “You know through the years it’s existed in iterations (in Houston), never within the context of a world class performing arts center that we believe brings a unique quality.

“And it brings us access to artists that otherwise might not say yes to making the trek to Houston. So it’s a really dynamic environment.”

Folkes mentions Dizzy’s Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center as a similar experience. Myron’s at the Smith Center in Las Vegas and Judson’s Live at the Dr. Phillips Center in Orlando are other comps. Folkes describes Houston’s club as “combining world class artists and performance with an elevated hospitality experience.”

Like those clubs, the new space will offer full bar and dinner options as well as with more than 150 performances each year. In the past year the Hobby Center hosted more than 450 performances reaching an audience of more than 475,000.

Holiday Decor

Swipe

“It’s an enormous reach,” Folkes says. “But what we’re excited about is that we’re going to make it even bigger.”

With $31 million of the campaign already realized, funds will cover or have covered state-of-the-art technology and fittings in both Sarofim Hall and Zilkha Hall, the transformation of audience areas including the Grand Lobby, Zilkha Hall Lobby, the box office, hospitality spaces and administrative offices. Concessions are being moved and a new bar will be added.

An addition in the hospitality arena is the Kades Club, named for significant campaign donors Mady and Ken Kades.

“This will be a place where we entertain certainly supporters during performances, but also creates a new event space that can be used for other events at the Hobby center as well,” Folkes notes.

The Kades foundation along with the Hamill Foundation and the Sarofim Foundation each contributed $5 million to the campaign.

Construction on all aspects of the project will begin in public spaces in late 2027 with all elements completed by fall 2028. Programming and events will not be interrupted during this time.

Joining in the fundraising effort are honorary co-chairs Marc Shapiro and Bill Wise, who led the original capital campaign to build the Hobby Center.

Supper Club Fun

So what will this new Houston supper club have? Let’s delve into some of the more interesting details:

— A  dedicated entrance

— A private, dedicated elevator

— A formal bar

— Seating arrangements for two, solo seating at the bar, banquette seating for five or six

— A new commercial kitchen

— Seating at stage level for 120

— Seating on the balcony level for 40

— The city skyline view will be maintained.

— Confirmed naming rights to be revealed in early 2027

— Gensler as architect and interior designer

— Charcoalblue as theater consultant

“We continue to be surprised at the level of excitement and interest we get from the artistic community,” Folkes says. “Yes, in Houston, but also across the country. And it is because of the signature of the Hobby Center for the Performing Arts.”

Young Texas Artists Bring an Unexpected Country Twist To Classic Cabaret, With Dosey Doe the Perfect Setting

Blankenship, Vonnahme and Malan Remind Audiences of Their Past Wins

By Laura Landsbaum // Oct 31, 2026

1/6

American soprano Brennan Blankenship, Voice Division gold medalist at the 2017 and 2019 Young Texas Artists Music Competition, performed at Classic Cabaret night. (Photo courtesy of Dave Clements)

Concert pianist Petronel Malan, a 1998 YTA gold medalist, returned to Classic Cabaret by popular demand on Oct. 18. Malan is a multiple-time Grammy nominee and gold medalist of several international piano competitions. (Photo courtesy of Dave Clements)

Cellist Cirdan Vonnahme, Classic Cabaret mistress of ceremonies Kelli Estes, Grammy-nominated South African pianist Petronel Malan, and soprano Brennan Blankenship. (Photo courtesy of David Hopper)

Cellist Cirdan Vonnahme, who received the Strings Division gold medal at the 2026 Young Texas Artists Music Competition, returned to perform at Classic Cabaret. He was accompanied by pianist Antonio Centenera. (Photo courtesy of Dave Clements)

Cris Woods, Bill Hazlett, and Lana Hazlett of The Woodlands attended the 2026 Young Texas Artists Classic Cabaret at Dosey Doe's big barn. (Photo courtesy of David Hopper)

Young Texas Artists Board of Directors members Ann McAlpin (left) of The Woodlands and Constance Gall Rhebergen are pictured with John Rhebergen. (Photo courtesy of David Hopper)

A Grammy-nominated pianist, an opera singer and a Rice University cellist helped Young Texas Artists launch its 42nd season at Dosey Doe with an unexpected country twist.

The annual Classic Cabaret night featured three performers who were winners at the annual YTA music competition. Young Texas Artists president and CEO Suzie Pokorski introduced the evening’s emcee Kelli Estes. Estes is the artistic, executive director and co-founder of Lone Star Lyric, the nonprofit opera and lyric theatre based in Houston.

The performances previewed the caliber of classical music talent audiences can expect in March at YTA’s annual Best of Texas concert, part of the Bach, Beethoven and Barbecue event. At the finalist concert, winners in four categories will share $40,000 in cash prizes plus career and performance opportunities.

American soprano Brennan Blankenship kicked off the night with two arias before tipping her hat to the Dosey Doe setting with a Willie Nelson tune. 

A Houston native, Blankenship founded Hopera, a Houston-based opera company that has introduced more than 5,000 Houstonians to the art form. Hopera aims to make opera more accessible, presenting English versions of opera classics in casual, craft brewpubs.

“At Hopera, we try to perform in places where regular Houstonians feel like they can come as themselves, dress however they want, be whoever they are, and come to our performances,” Blankenship tells PaperCity The Woodlands.”We have both free performances that we just try to catch whoever’s at the brewery to hear us play, just like any other musician.

Holiday Decor

Swipe

“And then we also do our ticketed operas, which are only $20. So that anyone can come.”

Cellist Cirdan Vonnahme is pursuing a bachelor of music in cello performance. He shared highlights from his emerging cello career. An Alaska native, Vonnahme noted that he took cello lessons via Zoom for more than nine years. He now relishes the opportunities to play with others.

“This summer I had the wonderful opportunity to play at Tanglewood, which is the (summer) home of the Boston Symphony,” Vonnahme says. “I got to share the stage with Yo-Yo Ma and the Boston Symphony cellists. And I got to play with the Boston Symphony in one of their concerts. And that was an experience I’ll never forget.”

Preparing For Life Outside the Concert Hall

Finally, Petronel Malan took to the stage and began her piano program, with some fascinating insight into Hungarian rhapsodies. The South African-born pianist is a Grammy nominee who began studying piano at age 4. Her program included works from Mozart, Liszt and Schütt, and ended with an unexpected encore.

Beyond her performance, Malan emphasized the importance of Young Texas Artist’s commitment to preparing musicians for careers beyond the concert hall.

“I mentor so many young students who I meet in masterclasses and conferences where I’m often the the conference opening concert,” Malan says. “And then I teach masterclasses to these young kids. In a music program, we learn everything about medieval music history.

“But it’s not the skills that you truly need in life. To file your taxes and do self employment taxes is a whole big game. And marketing and how to record a decent CD. Or how to write a biography.”

Through its annual competition and programs, Young Texas Artists helps emerging artists build the skills and opportunities to turn talent into lasting careers.

YTA’s Bach Beethoven and Barbecue event will be held in March of 2027. Applications are now open for the music competition.
